sowhat.text: With the 10-year at 5.10% and a December hike in play, debt stays expensive, but high yield spreads near 334 bp show credit is still open. A shaky tech tape can slow stock-funded deals, while energy and power asset sales keep getting done.

pitch: Stocks fell for a third straight day on Tuesday. The S&P 500 lost 1 percent to about 7,341, the Dow fell 1.6 percent, and the VIX rose to 25. Investors were waiting on Nvidia, which then beat estimates after the close and rose about 2 percent after hours. The 10-year Treasury closed at 5.10 percent, and stronger retail sales firmed bets on a December Fed hike. Oil edged up, with WTI near 86 dollars and Brent near 93. On deals, ECP closed its EnergySolutions buyout, Strathcona is buying Greenfire for roughly 2.7 to 2.9 billion Canadian dollars including debt, and NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for 4 billion dollars, with Barclays advising NRG.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury close on Tuesday 17 Nov?
Why did Nvidia rise after hours on 17 Nov?
quiz.a: It beat estimates: adjusted EPS of $2.68 on $115.84B of revenue, versus about $2.48 and $109.10B expected.

quiz.q: Who was lead financial adviser to NRG on selling six gas plants to LS Power, and for how much?

chat.a: Stocks fell a third straight day: the S&P 500 lost 1.0% to 7,341 and the VIX rose to 25.46. Investors were waiting on Nvidia, which beat estimates after the close. Rates are the backdrop, with the 10-year at 5.10%.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $86.01, up 0.3%, and Brent at $93.14, up 0.8%, a spread of about $7. I would not read much into a day this quiet. Lower oil helps consumers but weighs on upstream asset valuations, which matters for deals like Strathcona and Greenfire.
chat.tip: Say what would change your view.

chat.a: ECP closed its EnergySolutions buyout on 16 Nov, with Morgan Stanley and RBC advising EnergySolutions. Strathcona is buying Greenfire for about C$2.7–2.9B including debt, and NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for $4B at about 8.0x 2027 EBITDA, advised by Barclays.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: The FOMC minutes on Wednesday at 2pm ET, to see how committed the Fed is to another hike. I also want to see how Nvidia trades after its beat, since tech has been the main drag on stocks.
chat.tip: Tie each event to rates or AI spending.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 5.10% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration assets with most of their value in the terminal value are hit hardest.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How does a stock sell-off affect a sponsor deal like ECP and EnergySolutions?
chat.a: A falling S&P 500 and a VIX of 25.46 make buyers and sellers less sure on price, but sponsor deals depend mainly on debt cost and availability. High yield spreads were 334 bp on 16 Nov, so credit is open, though a 10-year at 5.10% makes the all-in cost high.
chat.tip: Separate equity volatility from credit access.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed range is 3.75–4.00% after a 25 bp hike in September, and stronger retail sales firmed bets on another hike in December. The 10-year is 5.10%, so debt is costly, but spreads near 334 bp mean credit is still available at a price.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
